title: Knowledge-Graph-Augmented Retrieval for Supply-Chain Event Impact Identification — MSc Dissertation
description: When a listed firm files an SEC Form 8-K, connected firms sometimes move abnormally too. I built a time-aware knowledge graph over 149 semiconductor, hardware and automotive firms (7 relationship types; 2,610 typed edges in the exported graph, 1,107 of them between the 149 firms; 1,444 approved by hand from 16,880 LLM-extracted candidates, each edge carrying its source and a valid-from date), pulled 6,608 8-K filings and labelled 5,873 under three abnormal-return benchmarks. I then tested a pre-registered protocol on 292 held-out events: BM25, dense and graph-hop hybrid retrieval, RAG, and a 4-bit QLoRA (RAFT) adapter on Llama 3.1 8B, trained on free Kaggle GPUs. Firms one hop from the filer were affected more often (+1.44 percentage points, one-sided p = 0.016, event-clustered bootstrap), but the effect was significant under only one of the three benchmarks. Graph-aware retrieval and fine-tuning made no measurable difference at fixed context, and a sector heuristic (F1 0.184) beat the best Llama system (F1 0.074) because recall was the bottleneck. I audited the evaluation code, fixed four bugs and traced an apparent fine-tuning regression to a context-construction confound.

title: MathGPT & BooleanGPT — GPT Transformers in PyTorch
description: Decoder-only GPT models written in PyTorch (no Hugging Face), adapted from the course's nanoGPT lecture code, to learn symbolic reasoning: arithmetic (MathGPT, 2.24M params, 78.2% exact match) and Boolean logic (BooleanGPT, 0.34M params, 98% exact match). Worked with self-attention, multi-head attention, positional embeddings and residual blocks, then analysed accuracy by operation (addition 84–87%, multiplication 68.7%), argued that network depth must grow with algorithmic complexity (O(n) addition vs O(n^2) multiplication), and tuned dropout against how deterministic each task is.

title: Temporal Signals of Deception — Fake News NLP
description: NLP study testing whether tense usage and temporal structure distinguish fake from verified news across 35,888 articles (ISOT dataset). Built a feature pipeline with spaCy (POS tagging, dependency parsing, tense and aspect classification), sentence-transformer and entity-grid coherence scores, and temporal-expression extraction. A classifier using only temporal and structural features reached 0.89 AUC with no word content, which suggests tense profile carries a real signal of deception in English news.

title: Game-Playing Agents — Minimax & Reinforcement Learning
description: Built and benchmarked three families of agents for Tic Tac Toe and Connect 4: Minimax with alpha-beta pruning and depth-limited search, tabular Q-Learning, and a Double DQN with experience replay in PyTorch, all against a rule-based baseline. Ran a 20,000-game round-robin tournament with a Tkinter GUI for interactive play. Alpha-beta pruning cut Tic Tac Toe search ~27x; depth-5 Minimax dominated overall (0.94 win rate), while RL agents beat their training opponent but overfit against tree search — a clear study of the search-vs-learning trade-off.

title: Response to City Disasters — Disaster Management Platform
description: Multi-user disaster management platform built over two semesters by a 10-person team using Extreme Programming: six two-week sprints, rotating driver-navigator pairs, double code review and test-first development. Stack: Java / Spring Boot backend, React 19 + TypeScript frontend, PostgreSQL on AWS RDS, ECS behind a load balancer, S3, SQS, Docker and GitLab CI/CD, with HERE Maps for routing. Civilians report incidents by form or voice and view shelters and evacuation routes; authorities get a validation engine that checks each report against weather, traffic, places, social-media and public-transport sources and assigns a confidence score, then review and dispatch. My contributions: the Emergency Response Team (ERT) resource-allocation engine (works out the units each agency needs from disaster type, severity and scale, routes the request through authority approval, then assigns the nearest Garda, Fire Brigade, HSE and Council units with cross-department substitution), a Grok-generated (xAI API) disaster summary report, the AI rerouting test cases and cross-service integration. In semester 1 I also gathered and integrated external APIs for the thin-slice build. I demoed the platform live.
highlights: Pair programming and double code review

title: LLM Multi-Agent Orchestration — Critical Review
description: Critical literature review (a written review, not a built system) of 18 papers (2023–2026) on how LLM-based multi-agent systems are orchestrated: centralised pipelines (MetaGPT, ChatDev), decentralised debate and ensembles (peer debate, Mixture-of-Agents), and learned or RL-optimised topologies (GPTSwarm, DyLAN, evolving orchestration). Compared each paradigm on reliability, scalability and cost, and traced the field's shift from hand-designed to learned orchestration.
context: Group literature review · Trinity College Dublin

title: CarsKG — Automotive Knowledge Graph
description: Semantic-web knowledge graph modelling the automotive industry — parent companies, manufacturers, car models, specifications and sales. Designed an OWL ontology (8 classes, 14 object + 15 data properties) with transitive, symmetric and inverse properties, transformed CSV data into RDF via RML mappings (28 car instances), authored 7 advanced SPARQL queries (aggregation, property paths, sub-queries) in GraphDB, validated data with SHACL shapes, and integrated external Linked Open Data sources.

title: OffScript — Adaptive Activity Recommender
description: Context-aware recommendation system that plans weekend activities by analysing a user's calendar workload, stated preferences and ongoing feedback. Uses a hybrid stereotype/overlay user model with a weighted preference vector and an 80/20 exploit-explore split to avoid filter bubbles, filtered by location, weather and free-time slots. Built with a React frontend, Python FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, and a scikit-learn recommendation engine integrating Calendar and Weather APIs.

title: Maze Pathfinding — Search vs MDP
description: Comparative analysis of six pathfinding algorithms — BFS, DFS, A* (Manhattan & Euclidean heuristics), Value Iteration and Policy Iteration — benchmarked across maze sizes from 10x10 to 100x100. Built a maze generator, an interactive Tkinter visualiser, and a metrics-logging system measuring path optimality, nodes explored and runtime. Showed classical search solves deterministic mazes ~100-6500x faster than MDP planners while both achieve optimal paths.

title: Lucene Search Engine
description: Java information retrieval system built on Apache Lucene (8.11.4), deployed on a Microsoft Azure Ubuntu VM, that indexes and searches the Cranfield Collection (1,400 abstracts, 225 queries). Benchmarked 25 analyzer/similarity combinations (Standard, Simple, English, Whitespace, Custom x BM25, Classic, Boolean, LM-Dirichlet, LM-Jelinek-Mercer) and evaluated with TREC Eval. BM25 with a custom analyzer gave the best retrieval effectiveness (MAP 0.425).

title: Full-Stack Web Scraper
description: MERN stack application with Puppeteer automating data extraction from web pages, improving data collection efficiency by 30%. Built during internship at gCurv Technologies.

title: Resume Analysis Web App
description: A Streamlit web app that analyses resumes using Pyresparser and provides personalised suggestions and tips to improve them.

title: TaskList — MERN Task Manager
description: A simple full-stack web app for recording and managing daily tasks, built with the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js).

title: Python Mini Projects
description: A collection of small Python projects and Jupyter notebooks exploring data analysis, automation, and algorithmic problem-solving.

title: Web Page Testing with Selenium
description: A Python-based test automation tool using Selenium for data validation and system reliability analysis with statistical checks for error detection.
